title: Common-stage shift descent core
statement: For finite coherent rational Verdier data F and a family t of integer shift structures on its finite dual functors, form the explicit shiftComponent by transporting each finite composite shift along descendedComparison and cancelling the opposite inclusion shift. Assume these components are natural on all pair-category arrows in every integer degree. Then they form a coherent integer CommShift on descendedDual, and all specified finite inclusion comparisons commute with these shifts. No exactness assumption on t is needed for this categorical assembly.

source.place: Coefficient transport: shift coherence for the explicit common-stage dual

proof.text: Transport the finite composite shift along descendedComparison. Cancel the opposite inclusion shift to obtain the explicit objectwise component. Its assumed naturality defines a natural isomorphism in every integer degree.

Precomposing the component with any opposite stage inclusion recovers the transported finite shift by cancellation. Verify that precomposition preserves isoZero and isoAdd, using the inclusion zero/addition laws and naturality. Every object lies literally in its own finite stage, so cancellation proves the global zero/addition laws.
The resulting composite shift agrees with finiteRestrictionShift in each degree. Transport compatibility of CommShift.ofIso gives the required NatTrans.CommShift on descendedComparison.
